dataset.title: MLCQ: Industry-relevant code smell data set

graphs.producerNote: CloudStack is the 9df5dcf3 release extraction, not a new candidate build.
CloudStack is the 9df5dcf3 release result; Eclipse is the earlier development extraction. Query this existing artifact without rerunning extraction.

interpretation: This known, purposively consensus-enriched cohort is development data, not a held-out test or population prevalence.
Do not tune a threshold or weights on the eight primary labels and claim independent success.
A large class span is not a god-object defect. Require responsibility/cohesion evidence and independent review before any diagnosis claim.
Do not alter the frozen Graphify environment, graphs, label votes, or prior native ranking outcomes.
Unequal graph producer versions and emitted-language coverage remain disclosed; this probe is only within each preserved Compass typed graph.

method.candidatePool: Every stored typed graph node with kind exactly class, a nonempty source file, and inclusive startLine/endLine with endLine >= startLine. No generated/test filter; exclude non-class kinds explicitly.
method.identity: For each annotated sample, require exact source file, exact simple Java class name (last codeName segment), and overlapping class/source line spans. Zero matches is unavailable; multiple matches are ambiguous. Never select nearest/best candidate.
method.outputs: Retain every class candidate identity/score/rank, all 55 join outcomes, primary positive/none retrieval separately, and bound/truncation failures. Preserve existing native Graphify and Compass hub results as separate controls.
method.score: Inclusive source span length = endLine - startLine + 1. Sort descending length, then ascending exact node ID. This is size, not responsibility/cohesion/defect severity.

purpose: Exploratory source-span ranking diagnostic for externally reviewed Blob classes; measure before considering a class-responsibility tool. This is not production behavior or a defect classifier.

samples.policy: Retain all 55 reviewed classes in selected revisions; four consensus-positive and four consensus-none primary cases. Other ratings remain uncertain/secondary, never converted to positive or negative.
